design_policy: Frozen independent predictions before execution. Designs use my own chemistry expectations; only CLI help and script parser syntax were consulted. No corpus, tests, or chemistry implementation were consulted for experiment inspiration. Unknown ingredient identities are naming/capability findings and require separate follow-up, not silent edits to these frozen predictions. A modeled outcome and an honest unsupported boundary are assessed separately.

experiments.title: Filter a dissolved electrolyte away from an inert mineral suspension
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NaCl 0.01mol
add v1 SiO2 1g
inspect v1
new
filter v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v2 conductivity
experiments.physical_expectation: Ordinary filtration retains particulate silica and passes water with dissolved sodium chloride. It must not treat all initially added solids as permanently filterable.
assessment_criteria: The receiver contains the mobile water/electrolyte pool; the source retains silica particles.
Total Na, Cl and Si inventories across source and receiver remain conserved.
Receiver conductivity is nonzero with an explicit supported or estimated model; unsupported silica identity is a separate naming/capability finding.

experiments.title: A pH electrode dipped into neat hexane must disclose its scope
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 hexane 20mL
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
measure v1 conductivity
look v1
experiments.physical_expectation: An ordinary aqueous pH value is not defined by putting a water-calibrated electrode into dry hexane. Hexane is a poor electrical conductor, but absence of an ion model is not proof of exact zero conductivity.
assessment_criteria: pH is explicitly unavailable or outside aqueous scope, rather than a confident neutral 7.
Any conductivity value distinguishes a modeled low response from missing ionic/conductivity data.
State inspection continues to identify hexane, with no invented water or proton reservoir.

experiments.title: A colorless metal salt should not acquire a fabricated visible spectrum
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 ZnSO4 0.001mol
inspect v1
measure v1 uvvis
look v1
experiments.physical_expectation: A dilute zinc sulfate solution is colorless in the visible range because Zn(II) has no visible d-d transition. This does not establish that its complete UV spectrum is zero.
assessment_criteria: Visible appearance is colorless or explicitly unresolved, without a copper-like color.
UV/visible output exposes missing wavelength/model coverage if a full zinc sulfate spectrum is absent.
No complete all-zero spectrum is asserted solely because a spectral entry is missing.

experiments.title: Evaporative concentration eventually leaves a conserved salt residue
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 20mL
add v1 NaCl 0.05mol
inspect v1
evaporate v1 0.9
inspect v1
measure v1 balance
look v1
experiments.physical_expectation: Removing 90% of solvent can make the remaining brine supersaturated and leave NaCl crystals. Sodium and chloride remain in the vessel; lost mass is attributable to escaped water, not salt.
assessment_criteria: NaCl analytical inventory remains 0.05mol through evaporation.
Reduced liquid-water inventory and any crystallization follow the same solvent removal.
Reported mass decrease agrees with explicit water loss; a missing saturation/evaporation model is disclosed rather than manufacturing or deleting salt.

experiments.title: Magnetic separation distinguishes iron filings from copper particles
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 Fe 0.01mol
add v1 Cu 0.01mol
inspect v1
new
magnet v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 balance
measure v2 balance
experiments.physical_expectation: A magnet attracts iron much more strongly than ordinary copper. The separation moves iron inventory while copper remains behind, without a chemical reaction.
assessment_criteria: The receiver gains the selected iron stock and the source retains copper.
Combined Fe and Cu mole totals equal their respective initial 0.01mol.
Combined mass is unchanged; no dissolved ions or reaction heat appear from magnetic separation alone.

experiments.title: Distillation should reject a nonvolatile electrolyte from the condensate
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NaCl 0.005mol
inspect v1
measure v1 conductivity
new
distil v1 v2 0.3
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v2 conductivity
experiments.physical_expectation: An ideal still carries volatile water into the receiver while sodium chloride stays in the pot. Salt concentration in the residue rises; entrainment is a separate mechanism, not implied by distillation.
assessment_criteria: Source and receiver NaCl totals close, with no NaCl transferred by the ideal vapor cut.
Receiver water is positive and source liquid-water inventory falls by the same amount.
Receiver electrolyte conductivity is much lower than the original brine, or the instrument explicitly discloses its missing low-ionic-strength model.

experiments.title: Fresh small solvent portions outperform one extraction with the same total solvent
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 I2 0.0001mol
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 I2 0.0001mol
new
new
inspect v1
inspect v2
extract v1 v3 hexane 0.1mol stages 1
extract v2 v4 hexane 0.1mol stages 4
inspect v1
inspect v2
inspect v3
inspect v4
experiments.physical_expectation: At the same distribution coefficient and total organic volume, several fresh equilibrium extractions remove more dissolved iodine than a single contact. Iodine conservation must hold separately for the two independent preparations.
assessment_criteria: The four-stage receiver contains more iodine and its aqueous source contains less than the single-stage pair.
Each source-plus-receiver iodine total remains 0.0001mol.
Any crystalline-capacity or coefficient-temperature boundary is disclosed; the comparison is not silently replaced by an unsupported empirical fit.

experiments.title: A dense organic liquid should leave through the lower-layer stopcock
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 20mL
add v1 CHCl3 10mL
inspect v1
look v1
new
drain v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 balance
measure v2 balance
experiments.physical_expectation: Chloroform is denser than water and only sparingly miscible with it. A simple two-layer separation therefore sends the chloroform-rich lower layer to the receiver, rather than assuming every organic layer floats.
assessment_criteria: Layer ordering follows density: chloroform-rich below water-rich.
A supported drain transfers the lower layer and leaves the upper layer, with total component inventories and mass conserved.
Unsupported chloroform phase-equilibrium data or identity must produce a clear capability finding, not an incorrect water-bottom default.

experiments.title: An acid-base indicator should reverse color after stoichiometric neutralization
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 phenolphthalein 0.000001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
look v1
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
look v1
inspect v1
experiments.physical_expectation: Phenolphthalein is pink in a moderately alkaline solution and loses that color when an equal strong-acid dose removes the excess hydroxide. Indicator dye is not irreversibly destroyed by this ordinary pH cycle.
assessment_criteria: Initial alkaline pH and indicator color are mutually consistent.
After equal HCl/NaOH amounts, excess alkalinity disappears and pink no longer persists.
Indicator analytical stock remains conserved; unsupported indicator identity or spectral equilibrium is separated from acid-base solver behavior.

experiments.title: Thiosulfate removes iodine color at two equivalents, not one
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 KI 0.001mol
add v1 I2 0.0001mol
inspect v1
look v1
add v1 Na2S2O3 0.0001mol
inspect v1
look v1
add v1 Na2S2O3 0.0001mol
inspect v1
look v1
experiments.physical_expectation: I2 + 2 S2O3(2-) gives 2 I(-) + S4O6(2-). One thiosulfate equivalent can reduce only half the original iodine; two equivalents exhaust it, while preserving all iodine and sulfur atoms.
assessment_criteria: After the first dose, reducible iodine remains; after the second, oxidized iodine is exhausted if this redox route is supported.
Iodine color tracks the remaining oxidized iodine rather than total iodine atoms.
Element/charge conservation closes through iodide and tetrathionate or the route explicitly reports missing chemistry instead of claiming a fictitious endpoint.

experiments.title: Carbonate acidification distinguishes bicarbonate storage from escaped carbon dioxide
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CaCO3 0.001mol
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
inspect v1
look v1
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
inspect v1
look v1
measure v1 ph
experiments.physical_expectation: Carbonate needs two strong-acid equivalents per mole for complete conversion to neutral carbon dioxide, but a one-equivalent dose may instead leave dissolved bicarbonate. A mineral disappearing is therefore not by itself proof that all carbon escaped as CO2. The second acid dose drives the carbon balance toward CO2 while conserving calcium.
assessment_criteria: The half-stoichiometric snapshot distinguishes residual carbonate, dissolved bicarbonate and reported CO2 instead of assuming disappearance means complete gas conversion.
At the full dose, original carbonate may dissolve with CO2 evolution or dissolved-carbon storage explicitly accounted for.
Calcium and carbon close across retained stock and reported boundary losses; pH is consistent with the remaining acid/base reservoirs.

experiments.title: A closed water freeze-thaw cycle should return its energy and matter
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 10mL
seal v1 100mL
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
cool v1 5kJ
inspect v1
look v1
heat v1 5kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v1 balance
experiments.physical_expectation: Five kilojoules is enough to freeze 10mL of initially room-temperature water. Adding back the same energy to an isolated closed vessel should restore its initial phase/temperature state approximately, with latent heat counted and no water lost to an open reservoir.
assessment_criteria: The cooling leg produces ice or explicitly discloses an unmodeled phase transition.
Final total water inventory and sealed material mass match their initial values.
Final temperature returns near the initial value if the same complete energy model supports both directions; a latent-heat gap must be visible instead of a confident false calorimetric closure.

experiments.title: An additional ideal stage enriches ethanol without creating it
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 0.5mol
add v1 ethanol 0.5mol
new
add v2 water 0.5mol
add v2 ethanol 0.5mol
new
new
inspect v1
inspect v2
distil v1 v3 0.1 stages 1
distil v2 v4 0.1 stages 2
inspect v1
inspect v2
inspect v3
inspect v4
experiments.physical_expectation: Below the ethanol-water azeotrope, a second ideal equilibrium stage can enrich the ethanol fraction of a small condensate cut relative to a one-stage cut. It cannot increase the pair total of water or ethanol.
assessment_criteria: Compute condensate ethanol mole fractions from inspected water and ethanol amounts; the two-stage cut should be richer than the one-stage cut.
Water and ethanol each close independently within their own source/receiver pair.
The stage model discloses its idealization and azeotropic limits, rather than extrapolating to pure ethanol without a boundary.

experiments.title: Diluting copper sulfate changes absorbance through concentration, not loss of copper
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.001mol
inspect v1
measure v1 uvvis
look v1
dilute v1 100mL
inspect v1
measure v1 uvvis
look v1
experiments.physical_expectation: For a dilute solution at unchanged optical path and nearly unchanged coordination chemistry, doubling solvent volume approximately halves absorbance of a fixed copper band. Copper atoms are conserved and the solution remains blue, but paler.
assessment_criteria: Copper and sulfate totals are unchanged while solvent volume approximately doubles.
At supported wavelengths, absorbance after dilution is approximately half its initial value, with fixed path length.
Missing copper spectral coverage is reported explicitly; color and quantitative UV/visible confidence are not conflated.

experiments.title: Half-neutralized acetic acid should reveal a buffer before equivalence
experiments.script:
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CH3COOH 0.01mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
add v1 NaOH 0.005mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
add v1 NaOH 0.005mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
experiments.physical_expectation: At half equivalence, an acetic-acid/acetate buffer has pH near pKa, about 4.76 at 25C. At complete neutralization, sodium acetate is mildly alkaline rather than exactly neutral; the conserved analytical acetate pool is 0.01mol.
assessment_criteria: Half-equivalence pH is approximately 4.5–5.1, conditional on temperature and activity scope.
Equivalence pH exceeds 7 and is higher than the half-equivalence value.
Acid plus acetate carbon inventory remains 0.01mol-equivalent; absent weak-acid hydrolysis/activity support is an explicit gap rather than a strong-acid shortcut.
